subject.title: [Feature]: Browser sandbox should support non-Docker backends (external CDP/noVNC endpoint)

question: Should OpenClaw add a narrow external CDP/noVNC endpoint config for sandbox browsers, or fold this into a broader browser-backend/plugin contract first?
rationale: The request changes public config and the browser-control security boundary, so automation cannot safely choose the endpoint trust model, lifecycle semantics, or long-term API shape.

options.title: Design versioned endpoint/backend contract
options.body: Add an explicit contract for externally managed sandbox browsers, including CDP auth, noVNC access, SSRF policy, validation, redaction, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader backend registry
options.body: Keep this issue linked to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/19289 and solve sandbox browser endpoints only as part of the browser backend/plugin API design.

options.title: Keep Docker-only for now
options.body: Document Docker as the only supported sandbox-browser backend until maintainers are ready to own the external endpoint security model.

recommendation.title: Design versioned endpoint/backend contract
recommendation.body: Add an explicit contract for externally managed sandbox browsers, including CDP auth, noVNC access, SSRF policy, validation, redaction, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete handled the related broad sandbox-provider closure and is the strongest available routing signal for the sandbox/backend security decision.
